degradation.modcrop: HR[:H - H % s, :W - W % s] (top-left anchored)

ablation_degradations.pil_bicubic_antialias: PIL.Image.resize((W // s, H // s), Image.BICUBIC) on the same modcropped HR

io.input: float32 tensor = uint8 / 255, shape (1, 1, h, w), range [0, 1]
io.rgb_baseline_input: gray replicated to 3 channels (upstream IMDN is RGB)
io.output: clamp to [0, 1], x255, round half to even (torch.round), uint8

metrics.psnr: 10*log10(255^2 / MSE), MSE over the border-cropped image, float64

ssim.reference: Wang et al. 2004, as skimage.metrics.structural_similarity(gaussian_weights=True, sigma=1.5, use_sample_covariance=False, data_range=255)
ssim.aggregation: mean of the SSIM map over the 'valid' region (window fully inside the image)

metrics.aggregation: mean over images of per-image values

speed.interleaving: for trial: for scale: for precision (thermal drift hits all configurations alike); the 5 x 300 samples of a configuration are pooled
speed.cooldown: before every trial, wait until the GPU is at or below cooldown_temp_c and the 1-minute CPU load average is at or below max_cpu_loadavg (at most cooldown_timeout_s), so trials start from a comparable state on a shared laptop; what was reached is recorded
speed.memory_format: default contiguous NCHW; no TensorRT, CUDA graphs or torch.compile
speed.fp32: float32 weights and activations, TF32 disabled
speed.fp16: automatic mixed precision: torch.autocast(float16), weights kept in float32 (as in threaded_display_60fps.py). Pure model.half() is not used: the channel-attention statistics overflow float16 on 160x128 and larger inputs and the output becomes NaN
speed.model_latency: input already on device; torch.cuda.synchronize() before and after each forward; wall clock via time.perf_counter
speed.end_to_end_latency: uint8 LR frame in host memory -> float conversion -> host-to-device copy -> forward -> clamp/round/uint8 -> device-to-host copy -> uint8 numpy frame (the copy back synchronises)

repo17.description: The 17 thermal frames committed in test-data/ (320x256, 8-bit grayscale).
repo17.source: FLIR ADAS v2 thermal images (Teledyne FLIR). The file names follow the dataset's naming (video-<id>-frame-<n>-<id>). Their size (320x256 = 640x512 / 2) and the realtime scripts that read them indicate they are the x2 bicubic LR versions of frames from this repo's own validation split (scripts/prepare-train-data.ipynb), copied in for the threaded demo.
repo17.licence: Teledyne FLIR Non-Commercial Image Dataset License Agreement (FLIR keeps ownership; research / non-commercial use). Not covered by this repository's MIT licence.
repo17.hr_note: The 'HR' reference here is itself a 2x bicubic downscale of the native 640x512 frame, so this set measures the operator on 320x256 content, not on native-resolution frames.

tno-lwir.description: Optional cross-sensor set: 51 single-band thermal images from the TNO Image Fusion Dataset (one per scene; image sequences excluded).
tno-lwir.source: Toet, A. (2014). TNO Image Fusion Dataset. figshare. https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.1008029 (Athena, DHV, TRICLOBS camera systems; 8-bit, from 359x247 to 945x709 pixels).
tno-lwir.licence: CC BY 4.0 (figshare record). Credit: TNO, Soesterberg, The Netherlands. Downloaded on demand to .bench-data/, never committed.
tno-lwir.hr_note: Native-resolution thermal images from cameras other than the one the model was trained on: a generalisation check, not an in-distribution test.
tno-lwir.selection: Selection: files whose name marks the thermal band (IR_*, ir, *_IR, IR<n>, *LWIR*) in single-scene folders; the FEL and DHV image sequences are excluded (near-duplicate frames). tank/LWIR.tif is excluded because its three channels differ (not a plain single-band image). APC_2 is excluded because its file names do not identify the band. The exact list and per-file SHA-256 are in benchmark/manifests/tno_lwir.json.

imdn_rgb_pretrained.label: IMDN, upstream RGB weights (no thermal fine-tune)
